learning_objective: 🎯 Learn how to measure, track, and analyze water usage at home or school to prevent waste and practice sustainable water management!

main_concepts.simple_explanation: A water audit is like a health checkup for water usage. It involves measuring exactly how much water enters a building, tracking where it gets used, and identifying where it is being wasted.
To manage water smartly, we need to count every drop. By calculating the water used for drinking, cooking, washing, and flushing, we can find out our average daily footprint.

A tiny, dripping tap can waste thousands of liters of clean water over time. Finding and repairing leaky pipes, faulty valves, and running flush tanks is a critical vocational skill in water management.
Once the audit shows where water is lost, we fix it! Simple steps like recycling kitchen wastewater for gardens and installing water-saving aerators on taps make a massive environmental impact.

fun_activity.title: 💧 The Home Leak Detective
fun_activity.instructions: Inspect every tap, pipe, and flush tank in your home for leaks. Place a dry bowl under a suspicious tap for one hour, measure any collected water, and calculate how much it would waste in a full day!

quick_recap: ⭐ A water audit tracks water inflow and consumption to build data-driven saving plans.
⭐ Detecting and repairing minor leaks is one of the fastest ways to prevent water wastage.
⭐ Modern water management relies on reducing consumption and recycling wastewater sustainably.
